mainTopic: Inheritance tracing back to the tribes, and the dispute with the צדוקים over whether a daughter shares the estate with the son's daughter
overview: The גמרא first explains how heirs are found when someone has no close relatives: you trace up the family tree, as far back as ראובן if needed. You never have to go further back to יעקב, because אביי says there is a tradition that a tribe never dies out completely. Then רב הונא, in the name of רב, rules that a daughter does NOT share the inheritance with the son's daughter, and anyone who says she does is following the צדוקים. A ברייתא proves this: the 24th of טבת was celebrated as the day the true law was restored over the צדוקים. In that story, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי demanded the צדוקים' source, and one old man answered with a קל וחומר: if the son's daughter inherits, surely the man's own daughter should. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answered with two פסוקים about צבעון and ענה, showing that a grandson is counted like a son. The גמרא asks whether there might have been two people named ענה, and answers from the words "הוא ענה" that there was only one. The צדוקי complains that he is being brushed off, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי begins his real answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How is the inheritance traced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the heirs are found when the deceased has no close descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short practical question about the earlier statement. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it was established that someone always has heirs, even with no children. The question is how we actually locate those heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How does this work?

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the clarification of the earlier rule about inheritance.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The method for finding heirs when there are no close relatives.

steps.title: Trace the family back as far as ראובן
steps.stepSummary: The inheritance is traced up the family tree, generation after generation, as far as ראובן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The inheritance keeps being traced back, step by step, all the way up to ראובן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: you keep climbing the family tree until you find living relatives, even going back as far as ראובן son of יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no close relatives exist, you go to the father's line, then the grandfather's, and so on. Some relative will always turn up somewhere along the line.

keyTerms.meaning: Keeps being searched out, traced step by step

phrases.english: The inheritance is examined and traced further and further,
up to Reuven.
phrases.notes: ראובן is just an example: for a family from any tribe, you trace back to that tribe's founding son of יעקב.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: You trace the family up through the generations, as far as the head of the tribe.

steps.title: Why stop at ראובן and not יעקב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the search stops at ראובן instead of going all the way to יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it say: up to יעקב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer: if the whole tribe of ראובן were gone, wouldn't you need to go up to יעקב and find relatives from the other tribes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stopping at ראובן assumes his descendants will always be around. The question is why we can assume that.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it say (a challenge: why not say it this way?)

phrases.english: But let it say: up to Yaakov!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that the search ends at ראובן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ראובן's line could die out, the search would have to go up to יעקב.

steps.title: A tribe never dies out completely
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that there is a tradition that no tribe will be wiped out entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that a tribe will never be completely wiped out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains that there is no need to go up to יעקב, because there will always be some descendants left in every tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every tribe always has survivors, you will always find an heir within the tribe. So ראובן is the furthest point you ever need to reach.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (we learned it as received teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: An inheritance always has an heir: trace up the family tree, and at the latest you will find relatives within the tribe, since a tribe never dies out.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We have a tradition that a tribe will not be wiped out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גְּמִירִי דְּלָא כָּלֵה שִׁבְטָא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tribe of ראובן might die out, so the search would need to reach יעקב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A tribe never dies out, so going up to the head of the tribe is always enough.

steps.title: Ignore anyone who says the daughter shares with the son's daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב rules that anyone who says a daughter inherits together with the son's daughter must not be listened to, since this is a view of the צדוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: Anyone who says that a daughter inherits together with the son's daughter, even if he is the נשיא of Israel, we do not listen to him, because this is nothing but a practice of the צדוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a strong ruling: the son's daughter takes the inheritance ahead of the deceased's own daughter, and the opposite view is rejected completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By our law, a son's descendants come before a daughter, so the son's daughter takes everything. The idea of splitting it between them comes from the צדוקים, so it is rejected no matter how important the person saying it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The son's daughter (granddaughter through a son)
Prince; head of the Jewish people
The Sadducees, a group that rejected the Oral Torah
We do not listen to him

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה: when a man leaves a daughter and a son's daughter, the son's daughter inherits everything.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר תִּירַשׁ בַּת עִם בַּת הַבֵּן,
phrases.english: Anyone who says a daughter inherits along with the son's daughter,
even if he is the prince of Israel,
we do not listen to him,
because these are nothing but the practices of the Sadducees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר תִּירַשׁ בַּת עִם בַּת הַבֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the order of heirs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter does not share with the son's daughter; that view is a צדוקי view and is rejected.

steps.title: Proof: a holiday marking the return to the true law
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that the 24th of טבת became a day of celebration when the true law was restored over the צדוקים' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: On the 24th of טבת we returned to our law, because the צדוקים used to say that a daughter inherits together with the son's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that this really was the view of the צדוקים, and that its defeat was celebrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proves רב's claim that the view comes from the צדוקים. The day the proper law came back was important enough to mark as a special day.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
On the twenty-fourth of Tevet we returned to our law.
For the Sadducees used to say:
The daughter inherits along with the son's daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בְּאַרְבָּעָה וְעֶשְׂרִים בְּטֵבֵת תַּבְנָא לְדִינַנָא
steps.raayaObject: That the view of a daughter sharing with the son's daughter belongs to the צדוקים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the 24th of טבת.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי challenges the Sadducees
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי confronts the צדוקים and demands their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי got involved with them and said: Fools, where do you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי challenges the צדוקים to show a source for their ruling. This sets up their reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not just disagreeing; he is demanding proof. The point is that their view has no real basis.

keyTerms.meaning: He took them on; he got involved with them

phrases.aramaic: נִטְפַּל לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai took them on,
he said to them: Fools,
where do you get this from?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְפַּל לָהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's story about the צדוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The צדוקים' ruling that a daughter shares with the son's daughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling needs a source, and they have none.

steps.title: An old man's קל וחומר for the daughter
steps.stepSummary: No one could answer except one old man, who argued with a קל וחומר: if the son's daughter inherits, surely the man's own daughter should.
steps.simpleTranslation: No one answered him a word, except one old man who babbled against him and said: If the son's daughter, who comes through the strength of his son, inherits him, then his own daughter, who comes through his own strength, surely should!
steps.whatsHappening: The צדוקים' only defense comes from one old man, who offers a logical argument for why the daughter should inherit too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument: the granddaughter is a step further away and only inherits through her father. The daughter is directly connected to the deceased, so she should have at least as strong a claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Through the strength of; by virtue of
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case

phrases.english: And there was no one who answered him a word,
except for one old man
who was babbling against him, and saying:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בַּת בְּנוֹ הַבָּאָה מִכֹּחַ בְּנוֹ – תִּירָשֶׁנּוּ;
phrases.english: If his son's daughter, who comes through the strength of his son, inherits him;

phrases.aramaic: בִּתּוֹ הַבָּאָה מִכֹּחוֹ – לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: his own daughter, who comes through his own strength, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הָיָה אָדָם שֶׁהֶחְזִירוֹ דָּבָר, חוּץ מִזָּקֵן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The צדוקים' reply to the challenge in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the daughter should inherit along with the son's daughter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the son's daughter to the daughter.

steps.title: The verse about צבעון and ענה
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers with two פסוקים: ענה is listed as a son of שעיר and also as a son of צבעון, which shows צבעון fathered ענה with his own mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: He read this פסוק about him: "These are the sons of שעיר the Horite, who lived in the land: לוטן, שובל, צבעון and ענה," and it is written: "These are the sons of צבעון: איה and ענה." Rather, this teaches that צבעון came upon his mother and fathered ענה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי responds to the old man by pointing out a contradiction between two פסוקים and resolving it. The discussion between them continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק makes ענה a son of שעיר, the other makes him a son of צבעון. The answer is that ענה was a grandson of שעיר, yet the פסוק counts him as a son, which hints that grandchildren stand in the place of children.
steps.confusionAlert: This verse is not yet the full rebuttal of the קל וחומר; the conversation continues right after this, so don't treat this as the final word.

phrases.english: He read this verse about him:
"These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who lived in the land:
Lotan and Shoval and Tzivon and Anah,"
and it is written: "These are the sons of Tzivon: Ayah and Anah"!
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:24. So is ענה צבעון's brother or his son?

phrases.english: Rather, this teaches

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבָּא צִבְעוֹן עַל אִמּוֹ, וְהוֹלִיד עֲנָה.
phrases.english: that Tzivon came upon his mother and fathered Anah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's response to the old man's קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Opens the rejection of the צדוקים' argument.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק counts a grandson (ענה) as a son, showing grandchildren stand in their parent's place, against the צדוקים' approach.

steps.title: Maybe there were two people named ענה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's inference: perhaps the ענה who was a son of שעיר and the ענה who was a son of צבעון were two different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe there were two people named ענה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story for a moment to poke a hole in the proof from step 9. Maybe the two פסוקים are talking about two different men who were both called ענה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 9 only works if both פסוקים refer to one person. If there were two people named ענה, then nothing shows that צבעון fathered a child with his own mother, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a possible alternative that would undo a proof)

phrases.english: But perhaps there were two people named Anah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוקים used in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's inference that one ענה was both the son and the brother of צבעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the name belongs to two different people, the פסוקים no longer show an incestuous birth, so the proof collapses.

steps.title: The words "הוא ענה" show it is the same ענה
steps.stepSummary: רבה (or, in another version, רב פפא) answers that the פסוק says "הוא ענה": this is the same ענה mentioned before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: I will say something that even "King שבור" did not say. Who is that? שמואל. Some say it was רב פפא who said: I will say something that even "King שבור" did not say. Who is that? רבה. The פסוק says "הוא ענה": this is the very same ענה from earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10. The extra words "הוא ענה" ("this is ענה") tell us it is the same person, not a second ענה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who gave this answer. In one, רבה says it, and "King שבור" means שמואל. In the other, רב פפא says it, and "King שבור" means רבה. Either way, the answer itself is the same: "הוא" points back to the ענה already mentioned, so there was only one ענה.

keyTerms.meaning: King שבור, used here as a title of honor for a great חכם
From before, the one mentioned at the start

steps.confusionAlert: "King שבור" is not the Persian king here. It is a nickname for a leading חכם: שמואל in the first version, רבה in the second.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
I will state a matter
that King Shapur did not state;
And who is he? Shmuel.
phrases.notes: "King Shapur" is a nickname. It means שמואל, a great חכם.

phrases.english: Some say: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמֵינָא מִלְּתָא דְּלָא אַמְרַהּ שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא;
phrases.english: I will state a matter that King Shapur did not state;
And who is he? Rabba.
The verse states: "This is Anah" —
he is the same Anah from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אָמֵינָא מִלְּתָא דְּלָא אַמְרַהּ שַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and confirms step 9's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reading: an extra word in the פסוק identifies the two people as one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The name ענה might belong to two different people.
steps.terutzMaskana: "הוא ענה" points back to the earlier ענה, so there was only one ענה.

steps.title: The צדוקי complains he is being brushed off
steps.stepSummary: Back in the ברייתא, the צדוקי protests that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer does not really deal with his argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, is this how you dismiss me?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא picks up again. The צדוקי says, "רבי, you're getting rid of me with this?" He feels the answer did not address his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקי treats the ענה answer as a way of brushing him off, not as a real reply to his קל וחומר. This sets up a direct answer from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

keyTerms.meaning: You dismiss me, send me off

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
phrases.notes: "He" is the צדוקי, speaking to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

phrases.english: with this you dismiss me?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי, בְּכָךְ אַתָּה פּוֹטְרֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story after the side discussion in steps 10–11 and objects to the answer in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer from the ענה פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer seems to sidestep the צדוקי's קל וחומר and does not answer it directly.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי begins his rebuttal
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers the צדוקי sharply, opening with "שוטה" (fool), as he begins his real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי starts his answer by calling the צדוקי a fool, and the actual argument continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sharp opening shows that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי sees the צדוקי's position as baseless. The content of his rebuttal comes right after this, so this step only opens the reply.

phrases.english: He said to him: Imbecile,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's response to the complaint in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The צדוקי's whole position, with the details continuing past this point.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated here. The content of the rebuttal comes on the next amud.
